01 BOTTOM LINE

FORECAST TrendForce forecasts global AR glasses shipments to more than double from 620,000 units in 2025 to 1.31 million in 2026 (111.1% YoY), led by Meta (~20% share) and four brands XREAL, Even Realities, Rokid and RayNeo (combined 53.2%), with nearly 80% further growth expected in 2027. ⟨cited figures: forecast; approximate⟩ C-43edca7ee80c70 C-8fc6400bb05f07 C-d241416a394058 C-721296f9609ab7 C-9bdb9c5f8edeee C-66860c5f782f79
SOURCE OPINION AR glasses are transitioning from proof-of-concept to consumer market, and brands are accelerating product development and channels to capture early demand. C-3ca90756e4869b C-3e1842d0cd420a
⚠ UNRESOLVED REVIEW — The cited opinion spans mention Meta's Ray-Ban Display momentum drawing consumer attention and primary drivers, but 'transitioning from proof-of-concept to consumer market' and 'accelerating product development and channels to capture early demand' are not stated in the cited spans.
MODEL INFERENCE Rising AR glasses volumes could benefit the named brands and their display/component supply chains, but the article does not quantify any listed-company revenue, margin or earnings effect, and three of the four non-Meta brands are private.

01 BOTTOM LINE

SOURCE OPINION The article documents that the S&P 500 sits less than 2% below all-time highs despite hot CPI/PPI prints and two-decade-high long-end yields, that equities historically compounded through long above-2% inflation regimes, and that consensus still calls for ~30% S&P 500 EPS growth. ⟨cited figures: forecast; approximate; approximate, read from a chart; data as of 2026-09-30⟩ C-eb7415654980c8 C-46ed2f40404587 C-8e1b1a28683e02 C-0a0845c8947bb9 C-d27f939f199c16 C-52df385b6c3f4d
SOURCE OPINION As long as earnings hold, equities can take hotter inflation and higher yields; if guidance shows weaker demand, margin pressure or rising financing costs, the same inflation data will matter much more. ⟨cited figures: forecast; approximate⟩ C-b783a6c88fd6f8 C-01d7456fe2691f C-8b0d5d56c271ab C-eea6d9a545ce50 C-8e1b1a28683e02 C-8376cfa7d8c9c0
MODEL INFERENCE The article's investable view is that inflation and yield levels matter little for equities until they show up in earnings; the research opportunity is to watch earnings and credit transmission rather than inflation prints alone, since a targeted above-2% regime is historically survivable.

01 BOTTOM LINE

SOURCE OPINION Morgan Stanley argues Canada's potential growth could rise from ~1.5% to 1.7% by end-decade and reach 2% in the 2030s, driven by productivity, efficiency and capital deployment, supported by abundant capital (pension assets 158% of GDP), a growing working-age population (+5% by 2040), and a capex cycle in which utilities, transport, mining and energy are ~61% of planned 2026 capex. ⟨cited figures: forecast; approximate⟩ C-63741952dd42c9 C-c43a89e092cc47 C-335c33c1eb61c9 C-607b3fda6b2238 C-0b564757852ce5 C-2bb63287013c7c C-6a1792a0b1c3d9
SOURCE OPINION The payoff should be faster growth, stronger corporate earnings and a more constructive outlook for Canadian assets, including a CAD strengthening to 1.36 from ~1.39. ⟨cited figures: forecast⟩ C-0c7c6a563260f6 C-479272006058e0
MODEL INFERENCE If the capital cycle broadens from structures/engineering into machinery, software and IP and productivity spreads, Canadian corporate earnings and the Canadian dollar could benefit; the article does not quantify the earnings effect.

01 BOTTOM LINE

FORECAST Morgan Stanley expects China to spend up to $12 trillion through 2035 on infrastructure, factory upgrades and new industrial capacity under its Industry 5.0 strategy, split roughly $0.5tn infrastructure, $5.5tn factory upgrades and $6tn new capacity. ⟨cited figures: forecast⟩ C-a01dc3d5e830dd C-cf7ce812a085e3 C-83381c2cb52c50 C-d683cf7b4a65fb C-7b79ec98d5831c
SOURCE OPINION The article says the spending may create opportunities for companies involved in automation, robotics, semiconductors, industrial software, power systems and next-generation manufacturing technologies, across three areas: infrastructure, factory upgrades and new capacity. ⟨cited figures: forecast⟩ C-adee5ed66e4a8a C-83381c2cb52c50 C-d683cf7b4a65fb C-7b79ec98d5831c
MODEL INFERENCE A multi-year, multi-trillion-dollar spending cycle would raise demand volumes for suppliers of automation, robotics, semiconductors, semicap equipment and industrial software, but the article names no specific listed companies and quantifies no supplier revenue effect.
